Main.sentence: Kenya , [a] officially the Republic of Kenya , [b] is a country located in ___E:East Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa)___ .

With an estimated population of more than 52.4 million as of mid-2024,  Kenya is the ___E:27th-most-populous country U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population)___ in the world  and the ___E:7th most populous U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_African_countries_by_population)___ in Africa.
Kenya's capital and largest city is ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ .

The second-largest and oldest city is ___E:Mombasa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa)___ , a major port city located on ___E:Mombasa Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa_Island)___ .

Other major cities within the country include ___E:Kisumu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu)___ , ___E:Nakuru U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakuru)___ and ___E:Eldoret U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldoret)___ .

Going clockwise Kenya is bordered by ___E:South Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan)___ to the northwest (though much of that border includes the disputed ___E:Ilemi Triangle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilemi_Triangle)___ ), ___E:Ethiopia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia)___ to the north, ___E:Somalia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia)___ to the east, the ___E:Indian Ocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean)___ to the southeast, ___E:Tanzania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania)___ to the southwest, and ___E:Lake Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria)___ and ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ to the west.

Kenya's ___E:geography U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Kenya)___ , ___E:climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_in_Kenya)___ and ___E:population U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Kenya)___ vary widely.

In western rift valley counties, the landscape includes cold, snow-capped mountaintops (such as Batian, Nelion, and Point Lenana on ___E:Mount Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya)___ ) with vast surrounding forests, wildlife, and fertile agricultural regions in temperate climates.

In other areas, there are dry, ___E:arid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arid)___ , and ___E:semi-arid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate)___ climates, as well as absolute deserts (such as ___E:Chalbi Desert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalbi_Desert)___ and ___E:Nyiri Desert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyiri_Desert)___ ).
Kenya's earliest inhabitants included some of the first humans to evolve from ancestral members of the genus ___E:Homo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo)___ .
Ample fossil evidence for this evolutionary history has been found at ___E:Koobi Fora U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koobi_Fora)___ .

Later, Kenya was inhabited by ___E:hunter-gatherers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter-gatherer)___ similar to the present-day ___E:Hadza people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadza_people)___ .

According to archaeological dating of associated artifacts and skeletal material, ___E:Cushitic speakers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Cushitic_languages)___ first settled in the region's lowlands between 3,200 and 1,300 BC, a phase known as the Lowland ___E:Savanna Pastoral Neolithic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna_Pastoral_Neolithic)___ . ___E:Nilotic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilo-Saharan_languages)___ -speaking ___E:pastoralists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism)___ (ancestral to Kenya's Nilotic speakers) began migrating from present-day ___E:South Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan)___ into Kenya around 500 BC.  ___E:Bantu people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_languages)___ settled at the coast and the interior between 250 BC and 500 AD.

European contact began in 1500 AD with the ___E:Portuguese Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire)___ , and effective colonisation of Kenya began in the 19th century during the ___E:European exploration of Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_exploration_of_Africa)___ .

Modern-day Kenya emerged from ___E:a protectorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_Protectorate)___ , established by the ___E:British Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire)___ in 1895 and the subsequent ___E:Kenya Colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony)___ , which began in 1920. Mombasa was the capital of the ___E:British East Africa Protectorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_Africa_Protectorate)___ ,  which included most of what is now Kenya and southwestern Somalia, from 1889 to 1907. Numerous disputes between the UK and the colony led to the ___E:Mau Mau revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_revolution)___ , which began in 1952, and the declaration of Kenya's independence in 1963. After independence, Kenya remained a member of the ___E:Commonwealth of Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations)___ .

The country's ___E:current constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kenya)___ was adopted in 2010, replacing the previous ___E:1963 constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kenya_(1963))___ .

Kenya is a ___E:presidential U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_system)___ ___E:representative democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representative_democratic)___ republic, in which elected officials represent the people and the president is the head of state and government.

The country is a member of the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ , ___E:the Commonwealth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations)___ , ___E:World Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank)___ , ___E:International Monetary Fund U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund)___ , ___E:World Trade Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization)___ , ___E:COMESA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COMESA)___ , ___E:International Criminal Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court)___ , as well as several other international organisations.
It is also a ___E:major non-NATO ally U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_non-NATO_ally)___ of the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ .

___E:Kenya's economy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya%27s_economy)___ is the largest in East and Central Africa, with Nairobi serving as a major regional commercial hub.  With a ___E:Gross National Income U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_National_Income)___ of $2,110,  the country is a ___E:lower-middle-income U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_country)___ economy.
Agriculture is the country's largest economic sector; tea and coffee are the sector's traditional cash crops, while fresh flowers are a fast-growing export.
The ___E:service industry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_industry)___ , particularly tourism, is also one of the country's major economic drivers.

Kenya is a member of the ___E:East African Community U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_African_Community)___ trade bloc,   though some international trade organisations categorise it as part of the ___E:Greater Horn of Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Horn_of_Africa)___ .
Africa is Kenya's largest export market, followed by the European Union.
The Republic of Kenya is named after ___E:Mount Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya)___ .
The earliest recorded version of the modern name was written by German explorer ___E:Johann Ludwig Krapf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Ludwig_Krapf)___ in the 19th century.

While travelling with a Kamba caravan led by the long-distance trader ___E:Chief Kivoi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Kivoi_Mwendwa)___ , Krapf spotted the mountain peak and asked what it was called.
Kivoi told him " Kĩ-Nyaa " or " Kĩlĩma- Kĩinyaa ", probably because the pattern of black rock and white snow on its peaks reminded him of the feathers of the male ostrich.
In archaic ___E:Kikuyu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gikuyu_language)___ , the word 'nyaga' or more commonly 'manyaganyaga' is used to describe an extremely bright object.

The Agikuyu, who inhabit the slopes of Mt. Kenya, call it Kĩrĩma Kĩrĩnyaga (literally 'the mountain with brightness') in ___E:Kikuyu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_language)___ , while the ___E:Embu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embu_language)___ call it "Ki-nyaga".
All three names have the same meaning.
Ludwig Krapf recorded the name as both Kenia and Kegnia .
Some have said that this was a precise notation of the African pronunciation /ˈkɛnjə/ .
An 1882 map drawn by Joseph Thompsons, a Scottish geologist and naturalist, indicated Mt. Kenya as Mt. Kenia.
The mountain's name was accepted, pars pro toto , as the name of the country.

It did not come into widespread official use during the early colonial period, when the country was referred to as the ___E:East African Protectorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_Protectorate)___ .
The official name was changed to the ___E:Colony of Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony)___ in 1920.

___E:Hominid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hominid)___ species, such as Homo habilis (fl. 1.8 to 2.5 million years ago) and Homo erectus (fl. 1.9 million to 350,000 years ago), possibly the direct ancestors of modern Homo sapiens , had lived in Kenya in the ___E:Pleistocene U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleistocene)___ epoch.
East Africa, including Kenya, is one of the earliest regions where modern humans ( Homo sapiens ) are believed to have lived.

In 1984, during excavations at Lake Turkana palaeoanthropologist ___E:Richard Leakey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Leakey)___ , assisted by ___E:Kamoya Kimeu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamoya_Kimeu)___ , had discovered the ___E:Turkana Boy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkana_Boy)___ , a 1.6-million-year-old Homo erectus fossil.

Further evidence of Kenya's prehistory was found in 2018, namely the early emergence of ___E:modern behaviours U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioral_modernity)___ , including long-distance trade networks (involving goods such as ___E:obsidian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obsidian)___ ), the use of pigments, and possibly the making of ___E:projectile points U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projectile_points)___ , about 320,000 years ago. The authors of three 2018 studies on the site suggest that complex and modern behaviours had already begun in Africa around the time of the emergence of Homo sapiens .

The first inhabitants of present-day Kenya were ___E:hunter-gatherer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter-gatherer)___ groups, akin to the modern ___E:Khoisan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khoisan)___ speakers.

These people were later largely replaced by agropastoralist ___E:Cushitic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cushitic)___ (ancestral to Kenya's Cushitic speakers), who originated from the ___E:Horn of Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_of_Africa)___ .
During the early ___E:Holocene U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocene)___ , the region's climate shifted from drier to wetter conditions.
This provided an opportunity for the development of cultural traditions such as agriculture and ___E:herding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herding)___ in a more favourable environment.

Around 500 BC, ___E:Nilotic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilo-Saharan_languages)___ -speaking ___E:pastoralists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism)___ (ancestral to Kenya's present-day Nilotic speakers) started migrating from what is now southern Sudan into Kenya.

Today, the country's Nilotic ethnic groups include the ___E:Kalenjin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people)___ , ___E:Samburu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samburu_people)___ , ___E:Luo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_(family_of_ethnic_groups))___ , ___E:Turkana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkana_people)___ , and ___E:Maasai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people)___ .

By the first millennium AD, ___E:Bantu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_languages)___ -speaking farmers had moved into the region, initially along the ___E:Kenyan coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenyan_coast&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .

The Bantus had originated in West Africa along the ___E:Benue River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benue_River)___ in what is now eastern ___E:Nigeria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria)___ and western ___E:Cameroon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon)___ .

The ___E:Bantu migration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_migration)___ brought new developments in agriculture and ___E:ironworking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_ferrous_metallurgy)___ to the region.

Today, the country's Bantu groups include the ___E:Kikuyu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people)___ , ___E:Luhya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhya_people)___ , ___E:Kamba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamba_people)___ , ___E:Kisii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gusii_people)___ , ___E:Meru U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meru_people)___ , ___E:Kuria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuria_people)___ , ___E:Aembu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aembu)___ , ___E:Ambeere U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambeere)___ , ___E:Wadawida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wadawida)___ -Watuweta, Wapokomo, and ___E:Mijikenda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mijikenda_peoples)___ , among many others.

Notable prehistoric sites in the interior of Kenya include the (possibly archaeoastronomical) site ___E:Namoratunga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namoratunga)___ on the west side of ___E:Lake Turkana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Turkana)___ and the walled settlement of ___E:Thimlich Ohinga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thimlich_Ohinga)___ in ___E:Migori County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migori_County)___ .

The coastline of Kenya was home to communities of ___E:ironworkers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironwork)___ and Bantu subsistence farmers, hunters, and fishers who supported the region's economy with agriculture, fishing, metal production, and trade with foreign countries.

These communities formed the earliest ___E:city-states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-states)___ in the region, which were collectively known as ___E:Azania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azania)___ .
The Swahili people were of mixed African and Asian (particularly Persian) ancestry, as ___E:DNA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)___ evidence has revealed.

By the 1st century CE, many of the area's city-states, such as ___E:Mombasa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa)___ , ___E:Malindi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malindi)___ , and ___E:Zanzibar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanzibar)___ , began to establish trading relations with the ___E:Arabs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs)___ .

This led to increased economic growth of the Swahili states, the introduction of ___E:Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ , ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic)___ influences on the ___E:Swahili language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_language)___ , ___E:cultural diffusion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_diffusion)___ , as well as the Swahili city-states becoming members of a larger trade network.

Many historians had long believed that the city-states were established by Arab or Persian traders, but archaeological evidence has led scholars to recognise the city-states as an indigenous development which, though subjected to foreign influence due to trade, retained a Bantu cultural core.

The ___E:Kilwa Sultanate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilwa_Sultanate)___ was a medieval ___E:sultanate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultanate)___ centred at ___E:Kilwa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilwa_Kisiwani)___ , in modern-day Tanzania.
At its height, its authority stretched over the entire length of the ___E:Swahili Coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_Coast)___ , including Kenya.
Beginning in the 10th century, the rulers of Kilwa would go on to build elaborate coral mosques and introduce copper coinage.

Swahili, a ___E:Bantu language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_language)___ with ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language)___ , ___E:Persian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_language)___ , and other Middle-Eastern and South Asian ___E:loanwords U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loanword)___ , later developed as a lingua franca for trade between the different peoples.

Since the turn of the 20th century, Swahili has also adopted numerous loanwords and ___E:calques U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calque)___ from English, many of which originated during the era of British colonial rule.
The Swahili built Mombasa into a major port city and established trade links with other nearby city-states, as well as commercial centres in Persia, Arabia, and even India.

By the 15th century, Portuguese voyager ___E:Duarte Barbosa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duarte_Barbosa)___ wrote that "Mombasa is a place of great traffic and has a good harbour in which there are always moored small craft of many kinds and also great ships, both of which are bound from ___E:Sofala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sofala)___ and others which come from ___E:Cambay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambay)___ and ___E:Melinde U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malindi)___ and others which sail to the island of Zanzibar."
One major city on the Kenyan coast is Malindi.

It has been an important Swahili settlement since the 14th century, and the city once rivalled Mombasa for dominance in the ___E:African Great Lakes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Great_Lakes)___ region.
Malindi has traditionally been a friendly port city for foreign powers.

In 1414, the Chinese trader and explorer ___E:Zheng He U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zheng_He)___ , representing the ___E:Ming Dynasty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_Dynasty)___ , visited the East African coast on one of his last ' ___E:treasure voyages U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_treasure_voyages)___ '.
Malindi also welcomed the Portuguese explorer ___E:Vasco da Gama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama)___ in 1498.

In the 17th century, the Swahili coast was conquered by the ___E:Omani Arabs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omani_Arabs)___ , who expanded the ___E:slave trade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_slave_trade)___ to meet the demands of plantations in ___E:Oman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oman)___ and Zanzibar.
Initially, these traders came mainly from Oman, but later many came from Zanzibar (such as ___E:Tippu Tip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tippu_Tip)___ ).

In addition, the Portuguese started buying slaves from the Omani and Zanzibari traders in response to the interruption of the ___E:transatlantic slave trade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transatlantic_slave_trade)___ by British abolitionists.

During the 18th and 19th century, the ___E:Masai people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masai_people)___ moved into the central and southern ___E:Rift Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya)___ plains of Kenya, from a region north of Lake Rudolf (now ___E:Lake Turkana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Turkana)___ ).

Although there weren't many of them, they managed to conquer a great amount of land in the plains, where people did not put up much resistance. [citation needed] The ___E:Nandi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandi_people)___ peoples managed to oppose the Masai, while the Taveta peoples fled to the forests on the eastern edge of ___E:Mount Kilimanjaro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kilimanjaro)___ , although they later were forced to leave the land due to the threat of ___E:smallpox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox)___ .

An outbreak of either ___E:rinderpest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinderpest)___ or ___E:pleuropneumonia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleuropneumonia)___ greatly affected the Masai's cattle, while an epidemic of smallpox affected the Masai themselves.
After the death of the Masai ___E:Mbatian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mbatian)___ , the chief laibon (medicine man), the Masai split into warring factions.

The Masai caused much strife in the areas they conquered; however, cooperation between such groups as the ___E:Luo people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_people)___ , ___E:Luhya people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhya_people)___ , and ___E:Gusii people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gusii_people)___ is evidenced by shared vocabulary for modern implements and similar economic regimes.
Although Arab traders remained in the area, trade routes were disrupted by the hostile Masai, though there was trade in ivory between these factions.

The first foreigners to successfully get past the Masai were ___E:Johann Ludwig Krapf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Ludwig_Krapf)___ and ___E:Johannes Rebmann U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Rebmann)___ , two German missionaries who established a mission in ___E:Rabai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabai)___ , not too far from ___E:Mombasa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa)___ .
The pair were the first Europeans to sight ___E:Mount Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya)___ .

The ___E:German Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Empire)___ established a protectorate over the ___E:Sultan of Zanzibar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan_of_Zanzibar)___ 's coastal possessions in 1885, followed by the arrival of the ___E:Imperial British East Africa Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_British_East_Africa_Company)___ in 1888. Imperial rivalry was prevented by the ___E:Heligoland–Zanzibar Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heligoland%E2%80%93Zanzibar_Treaty)___ , so Germany handed its East African coastal holdings to Britain in 1890.
The transfer by Germany to Britain was followed by the building of the ___E:Uganda Railway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Railway)___ passing through the country.

The building of the railway was resisted by some ethnic groups—notably the ___E:Nandi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandi_people)___ , led by Orkoiyot ___E:Koitalel Arap Samoei U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koitalel_Arap_Samoei)___ from 1890 to 1900—but the British eventually built it. The Nandi were the first ethnic group to be put in a native reserve to stop them from disrupting the building of the railway.
During the railway construction era, there was a significant influx of Indian workers, who provided the bulk of the skilled labour required for construction.

They and most of their descendants later remained in Kenya and formed the core of several distinct Indian communities, such as the ___E:Ismaili Muslim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismailism)___ and ___E:Sikh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh)___ communities.

Following general elections held in 1997, the Constitution of Kenya Review Act, designed to pave the way for more comprehensive amendments to the Kenyan constitution, was passed by the national parliament.

Under the new constitution and with President Kibaki prohibited by term limits from running for a third term, Deputy Prime Minister ___E:Uhuru Kenyatta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uhuru_Kenyatta)___ ran for office.
He won with 50.51% of the vote in March 2013.

Kenya has close ties with its fellow ___E:Swahili U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_language)___ -speaking neighbours in the ___E:African Great Lakes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Great_Lakes)___ region.

The ___E:President of Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Kenya)___ is the ___E:commander-in-chief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-chief)___ of all the armed forces.

Further, in the aftermath of the national elections of December 2007 and the violence that subsequently engulfed the country, a commission of inquiry, the ___E:Waki Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waki_Commission)___ , commended its readiness and adjudged it to "have performed its duty well."  Nevertheless, there have been serious allegations of human rights violations, most recently while conducting counter-insurgency operations in the ___E:Mt Elgon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mt_Elgon)___ area  and also in the district of ___E:Mandera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandera)___ central.
Kenya's armed forces, like many government institutions in the country, have been tainted by ___E:corruption U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corruption_in_Kenya)___ allegations.

Because the operations of the armed forces have been traditionally cloaked by the ubiquitous blanket of "state security", the corruption has been hidden from public view, and thus less subject to public scrutiny and notoriety.
This has changed recently.
In what are by Kenyan standards unprecedented revelations, in 2010, credible claims of corruption were made with regard to recruitment  and procurement of armoured personnel carriers.
Further, the wisdom and prudence of certain decisions of procurement have been publicly questioned.
Kenya is divided into ___E:47 semi-autonomous counties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counties_of_Kenya)___ that are headed by governors.

Locations are usually named after their central villages/towns.
Many larger towns consist of several locations.
Each location has a chief, appointed by the state.

An interim boundaries commission was formed in 2010 to review the constituencies and in its report, it recommended the creation of an additional 80 constituencies.

___E:Homosexual acts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality)___ are illegal in Kenya and typically punishable by up to 14 years in prison.
According to a 2020 survey by the ___E:Pew Research Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center)___ , 83% of Kenyans believe that homosexuality should not be accepted by society.

While addressing a joint press conference together with President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ in 2015, President Kenyatta declined to assure Kenya's commitment to gay rights, saying that "the issue of gay rights is really a non-issue...
But there are some things that we must admit we don't share.
Our culture, our societies don't accept."

In November 2008, ___E:WikiLeaks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks)___ brought wide international attention to The Cry of Blood report, which documents the extrajudicial killing of gangsters by the Kenyan police.

In the report, the ___E:Kenya National Commission on Human Rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_National_Commission_on_Human_Rights)___ (KNCHR) reported these in their key finding "e)", stating that the ___E:forced disappearances U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forced_disappearance)___ and ___E:extrajudicial killings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extrajudicial_killing)___ appeared to be official policy sanctioned by the political leadership and the police.

Kenya's ___E:macroeconomic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macroeconomics)___ outlook has steadily posted robust growth over the past few decades mostly from ___E:road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road)___ , ___E:rail U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rail_transport)___ , ___E:air U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-cost_carrier)___ and ___E:water transport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_transport)___ infrastructure projects as well as massive investments in ___E:Information and Communication Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_and_communications_technology)___ .
The Kenyan economy is the largest in East Africa.
After independence, Kenya promoted rapid economic growth through public investment, encouraged smallholder agricultural production and provided incentives for private industrial investment.

Kenya is East Africa's regional transportation and financial hub. Kenya's financial sector is vibrant, well developed and diversified boasting the highest financial inclusion in the region and globally.
Foreign investments in Kenya remain relatively weak considering the size of its economy and its level of development.
As of 2022, Kenya's total FDI stock stood at US$10.4 billion, accounting for a mere 9.5% of the country's GDP.
Kenya has a ___E:Human Development Index U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index)___ (HDI) of 0.628 (medium), ranked 143 out of 193 in the world as of 2023 [update] .

As of 2022, 25.4% of Kenyans lived on less than $2.15 a day.  Based on the most recent data from 2022, 25.4% of the population is affected by ___E:multidimensional poverty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multidimensional_Poverty_Index)___ and an additional 26.4% vulnerable to it.   In 2017, Kenya ranked 92nd in the World Bank ___E:ease of doing business U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ease_of_doing_business_index)___ rising from 113rd in 2016 (of 190 countries).
The important agricultural sector employs around 30% of the workforce.

Kenya is usually classified as a ___E:frontier market U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontier_market)___ or occasionally an ___E:emerging market U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerging_market)___ , and is one of the ___E:Developing countries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_country)___ .

The economy has seen much expansion, seen by strong performance in tourism, higher education and ___E:telecommunications U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecommunications_in_Kenya)___ and decent post-drought results in agriculture, especially the vital tea sector.
Kenya's economy grew by more than 7% in 2007, and its foreign debt was greatly reduced.
This changed immediately after the disputed presidential election of December 2007, following the chaos which engulfed the country.

Telecommunications and financial activity over the last decade now comprise 62% of GDP. 22% of GDP still comes from the unreliable agricultural sector which employs 75% of the labour force (a characteristic of under-developed economies that have not attained ___E:food security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security)___ ).

A small portion of the population relies on food aid.  Industry and manufacturing is the smallest sector, accounting for 16% of GDP. The services, industry and manufacturing sectors only employ 25% of the labour force but contribute 75% of GDP.  Kenya also exports textiles worth over $400 million under ___E:AGOA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AGOA)___ .

Privatisation of state corporations like the defunct Kenya Post and Telecommunications Company, which resulted in East Africa's most profitable company— ___E:Safaricom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safaricom)___ , has led to their revival because of massive private investment.

As of May 2011 [update] , economic prospects are positive with 4–5% GDP growth expected, largely because of expansions in ___E:tourism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism)___ , ___E:telecommunications U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecommunications)___ , transport, construction, and a recovery in ___E:agriculture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture)___ .
The ___E:World Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank)___ estimated growth of 4.3% in 2012.
In March 1996 the presidents of Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda re-established the ___E:East African Community U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_African_Community)___ (EAC).
The EAC's objectives include harmonising tariffs and customs regimes, free movement of people and improving regional infrastructures.
In March 2004, the three East African countries signed a ___E:Customs Union Agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customs_union)___ .
Kenya has a more developed financial services sector than its neighbours.
The ___E:Nairobi Securities Exchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_Securities_Exchange)___ (NSE) is ranked 4th in Africa in terms of market capitalisation.
The Kenyan banking system is supervised by the ___E:Central Bank of Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Kenya)___ (CBK).

As of late July 2004, the system consisted of 43 commercial banks (down from 48 in 2001) and several ___E:non-bank financial institutions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-bank_financial_institution)___ including mortgage companies, four savings and loan associations and several core foreign-exchange bureaus.
The inaugural Kenya Innovation Week (KIW) was started in 2021, from December 6 to 10, 2021, at the Kenya School of Government in Lower Kabete, Nairobi.

Tourism contributes around 6% to Kenya's economy.  ___E:Tourism in Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_Kenya)___ is the third-largest source of foreign exchange revenue following diaspora remittances and agriculture.
The Kenya Tourism Board is responsible for maintaining information pertaining to tourism in Kenya.
The main tourist attractions are photo safaris through the ___E:60 national parks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_national_parks_of_Kenya)___ and game reserves.

Game reserves include ___E:Maasai Mara Game Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_Mara_Game_Reserve)___ , ___E:Samburu National Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samburu_National_Reserve)___ , ___E:Solio Game Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solio_Game_Reserve)___ , ___E:Shaba National Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaba_National_Reserve)___ , ___E:Buffalo Springs National Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Springs_National_Reserve)___ among others.

Other attractions include the ___E:wildebeest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildebeest)___ migration at the ___E:Masaai Mara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaai_Mara)___ , which is considered to be the 7th wonder of the world; historical mosques, and colonial-era forts at ___E:Mombasa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa)___ , ___E:Malindi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malindi)___ , and ___E:Lamu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamu)___ ; renowned scenery such as the white-capped ___E:Mount Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya)___ and the ___E:Great Rift Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya)___ ; tea plantations at ___E:Kericho U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kericho)___ ; coffee plantations at ___E:Thika U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thika)___ ; a splendid view of ___E:Mount Kilimanjaro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kilimanjaro)___ across the border into Tanzania; and the beaches along the ___E:Swahili Coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_Coast)___ , in the ___E:Indian Ocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean)___ .

Tourists, the largest number being from ___E:Germany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany)___ and the ___E:United Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom)___ , are attracted mainly to the coastal beaches and the ___E:game reserves U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_reserve)___ , notably, the expansive ___E:East U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsavo_East_National_Park)___ and ___E:Tsavo West National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsavo_West_National_Park)___ , 20,808 square kilometres (8,034 sq mi) to the southeast. Agriculture is the second largest contributor to Kenya's gross domestic product (GDP) after the service sector.

In 2005, agriculture, including ___E:forestry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forestry)___ and fishing, accounted for 24% of GDP, as well as for 18% of wage employment and 50% of revenue from exports.
The principal ___E:cash crops U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cash_crop)___ are tea, horticultural produce, and coffee.
Horticultural produce and tea are the main growth sectors and the two most valuable of all of Kenya's exports.
The production of major food staples such as ___E:corn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize)___ is subject to sharp weather-related fluctuations.
Production downturns periodically necessitate food aid—for example in 2004, due to one of Kenya's intermittent ___E:droughts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Droughts)___ .

A consortium led by the ___E:International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Crops_Research_Institute_for_the_Semi-Arid_Tropics)___ ( ___E:ICRISAT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICRISAT)___ ) has had some success in helping farmers grow new ___E:pigeon pea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigeon_pea)___ varieties instead of maize, in particularly dry areas.
Pigeon peas are very drought-resistant, so can be grown in areas with less than 650 millimetres (26 in) annual rainfall.
Successive projects encouraged the commercialisation of legumes by stimulating the growth of local seed production and agro-dealer networks for distribution and marketing.
This work, which included linking producers to wholesalers, helped to increase local producer prices by 20–25% in Nairobi and Mombasa.

The commercialisation of the pigeon pea is now enabling some farmers to buy assets ranging from mobile phones to productive land and livestock, and is opening pathways for them to move out of poverty.
Tea, coffee, sisal, pyrethrum, corn, and wheat are grown in the fertile highlands, one of the most successful agricultural production regions in Africa.

Livestock predominates in the semi-arid savanna to the north and east. ___E:Coconuts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconuts)___ , ___E:pineapples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pineapples)___ , ___E:cashew nuts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cashew_nuts)___ , cotton, ___E:sugarcane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarcane)___ , ___E:sisal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisal)___ , and corn are grown in the lower-lying areas.

Kenya has not attained the level of investment and efficiency in agriculture that can guarantee food security, and coupled with resulting poverty (53% of the population lives below the poverty line), a significant portion of the population regularly starves and is heavily dependent on food aid.  Poor roads, an inadequate railway network, under-used water transport, and expensive air transport have isolated mostly ___E:arid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arid)___ and ___E:semi-arid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid)___ areas, and farmers in other regions often leave food to rot in the fields because they cannot access markets.

This was last seen in August and September 2011, prompting the ___E:Kenyans for Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyans_for_Kenya)___ initiative by the ___E:Red Cross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cross)___ .

Kenya's ___E:irrigation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrigation)___ sector is categorised into three organizational types: ___E:smallholder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallholding)___ schemes, centrally-managed public schemes, and private/commercial irrigation schemes.
The smallholder schemes are owned, developed, and managed by individuals or groups of farmers operating as water users or self-help groups.

Irrigation is carried out on individual or on group farms averaging 0.1–0.4 ha. There are about 3,000 smallholder irrigation schemes covering a total area of 47,000 ha. The country has seven large, centrally managed irrigation schemes, namely Mwea, ___E:Bura U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bura_irrigation_and_Settlement_Project_(Kenya))___ , ___E:Hola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hola,_Kenya)___ , ___E:Perkera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perkerra_River)___ , West Kano, Bunyala, and ___E:Ahero U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahero)___ , covering a total area of 18,200 ha and averaging 2,600 ha per scheme.
These schemes are managed by the National Irrigation Board and account for 18% of irrigated land area in Kenya.

Large-scale private commercial farms cover 45,000 hectares, accounting for 40% of irrigated land. They utilise high technology and produce high-value crops for the export market, especially flowers and vegetables.
Kenya is the world's 3rd largest exporter of ___E:cut flowers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cut_flowers)___ .
Roughly half of Kenya's 127 flower farms are concentrated around ___E:Lake Naivasha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Naivasha)___ , 90 kilometres northwest of Nairobi.
To speed their export, Nairobi airport has a terminal dedicated to the transport of flowers and vegetables.

Although Kenya is a low middle-income country, manufacturing accounts for 14% of the GDP, with industrial activity concentrated around the three largest urban centres of ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ , ___E:Mombasa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa)___ , and ___E:Kisumu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu)___ , and is dominated by food-processing industries such as grain milling, beer production, sugarcane crushing, and the fabrication of consumer goods, e.g., vehicles from kits.
Kenya also has a cement production industry.
Kenya has an ___E:oil refinery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_refinery)___ that processes imported crude petroleum into petroleum products, mainly for the domestic market.

In addition, a substantial and expanding ___E:informal sector U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Informal_sector)___ commonly referred to as jua kali engages in small-scale manufacturing of household goods, auto parts, and farm implements.

Kenya's inclusion among the beneficiaries of the US Government's African Growth and Opportunity Act ( ___E:AGOA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AGOA)___ ) has given a boost to manufacturing in recent years.
Since AGOA took effect in 2000, Kenya's clothing sales to the United States increased from US$44 million to US$270 million (2006).
Other initiatives to strengthen manufacturing have been the new government's favourable tax measures, including the removal of duty on capital equipment and other raw materials.

In 2023, Kenya is in the process of constructing five industrial parks that will operate tax-free, with an anticipated completion date set for 2030. There are intentions to develop an additional 20 industrial parks in the future.

Two trans-African automobile routes pass through Kenya: the ___E:Cairo-Cape Town Highway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairo-Cape_Town_Highway)___ and the ___E:Lagos-Mombasa Highway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos-Mombasa_Highway)___ , so the country has an extensive road network of paved and unpaved roads.
Kenya's railway system links the nation's ports and major cities, connecting it with neighbouring Uganda.
There are 15 airports which have paved runways.

The largest share of Kenya's electricity supply comes from geothermal energy,  followed by hydroelectric stations at dams along the upper ___E:Tana River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tana_River_(Kenya))___ , as well as the Turkwel Gorge Dam in the west. A petroleum-fired plant on the coast, ___E:geothermal facilities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geothermal_power_in_Kenya)___ at ___E:Olkaria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olkaria)___ (near Nairobi), and electricity imported from ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ make up the rest of the supply.
A ___E:2,000 MW powerline from Ethiopia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodo%E2%80%93Moyale%E2%80%93Suswa_High_Voltage_Power_Line)___ was completed in 2022.

Kenya's installed capacity increased from 1,142 ___E:megawatts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megawatts)___ between 2001 and 2003 to 2,341 in 2016.  The state-owned ___E:Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Electricity_Generating_Company)___ , established in 1997 under the name of Kenya Power Company, handles the generation of electricity, ___E:Kenya Electricity Transmission Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Electricity_Transmission_Company)___ handles long distance distribution of electricity, while ___E:Kenya Power and Lighting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Power_and_Lighting)___ handles the electricity transmission and distribution system in the country.

Shortfalls of electricity occur periodically, when drought reduces water flow. To become energy sufficient, Kenya has installed ___E:wind power U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_power_in_Kenya)___ and ___E:solar power U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_power_in_Kenya)___ (over 300 MW each), and aims to build a nuclear power plant by 2027.

Kenya has proven deposits of oil in ___E:Turkana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkana_County)___ . ___E:Tullow Oil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tullow_Oil)___ estimates the country's oil reserves to be around one billion barrels.
Exploration is still continuing to determine whether there are more reserves.
Kenya currently imports all crude petroleum requirements.

Since 2013 the government resorted to importing processed white petroleum. ___E:Kenya Pipeline Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Pipeline_Company)___ is the state-owned parastatal mandated with the storage and transportation of white petroleum.
The company was recently privatized by the government with the government owning a minor stake.
Kenya has no strategic reserves and relies solely on oil marketers' 21-day oil reserves required under industry regulations.
Petroleum accounts for 20% to 25% of the national import bill.

Published comments on Kenya's ___E:Capital FM U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/98.4_Capital_FM)___ website by Liu Guangyuan, ___E:China's ambassador to Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Ambassador_to_Kenya)___ , at the time of President Kenyatta's 2013 trip to Beijing, said, "Chinese investment in Kenya ... reached $474 million, representing Kenya's largest source of foreign direct investment, and ... bilateral trade ... reached $2.84 billion" in 2012. Kenyatta was "[a]ccompanied by 60 Kenyan business people [and hoped to] ... gain support from China for a planned $2.5 billion railway from the southern Kenyan port of Mombasa to neighbouring Uganda, as well as a nearly $1.8 billion dam", according to a statement from the president's office, also at the time of the trip.
Base Titanium, a subsidiary of Base resources of Australia, shipped its first major consignment of minerals to China.
About 25,000 tonnes of ___E:ilmenite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilmenite)___ was flagged off the Kenyan coastal town of Kilifi.
The first shipment was expected to earn Kenya about KSh.15–20 billion/= in earnings.
In 2014, the Chinese contracted railway project from Nairobi to Mombasa was suspended due to a dispute over compensation for land acquisition.

In 2007, the Kenyan government unveiled ___E:Vision 2030 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Vision_2030)___ , an economic development programme it hopes will put the country in the same league as the ___E:Asian Economic Tigers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Asian_Tigers)___ by 2030. In 2013, it launched a National Climate Change Action Plan, having acknowledged that omitting climate as a key development issue in Vision 2030 was an oversight failure.

The 200-page Action Plan, developed with support from the ___E:Climate & Development Knowledge Network U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_%26_Development_Knowledge_Network)___ , sets out the Government of Kenya's vision for a 'low-carbon climate resilient development pathway'.

At the launch in March 2013, the Secretary of the Ministry of Planning, National Development, and Vision 2030 emphasized that climate would be a central issue in the renewed Medium-Term Plan that would be launched in the coming months.
This would create a direct and robust delivery framework for the Action Plan and ensure climate change is treated as an economy-wide issue.

Health care is one of the low-priority sectors in Kenya and was allocated 4.8% of the national budget in 2019/2020 or just 4.59% of ___E:GDP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP)___ compared to high-priority sectors such as education which was allocated more than 25%.
This is below the 4.98% average in ___E:Sub-Saharan Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-Saharan_Africa)___ and 9.83% spent globally.

According to the National and County Health Budget Analysis FY 2020/21, the breakdown of county health expenditure was 58% on Policy Planning and Administrative Support Services, 28% on Curative and Rehabilitative Health Services, 8% on Preventive and Promotive Health Services and 7% on Other Programmes.

Health care is largely funded by private individuals and their families or employers through direct payments to ___E:health care providers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_provider)___ , to the ___E:National Health Insurance Fund U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hospital_Insurance_Fund)___ or to medical insurance companies.

Public hospitals are ___E:fee-for-service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fee-for-service)___ establishments that generate large amounts of county and national government revenues making them highly political and corrupt enterprises.

Private health facilities are diverse, highly dynamic, and difficult to classify, unlike public health facilities, which are easily grouped in classes that consist of community-based (level I) services, run by ___E:community health workers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_health_worker)___ ; dispensaries (level II facilities) run by ___E:nurses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nurse)___ ; health centres (level III facilities), run by ___E:clinical officers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_officer)___ ; sub-county hospitals (level IV facilities), which may be run by a ___E:clinical officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_officer)___ or a ___E:medical officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_practitioner)___ ; county hospitals (level V facilities), which may be run by a ___E:medical officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_practitioner)___ or a ___E:medical practitioner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consultant_(medicine))___ ; and national referral hospitals (level VI facilities), which are run by fully qualified ___E:medical practitioners U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consultant_(medicine))___ .

Children attend nursery school, or kindergarten in the private sector until they are five years old. This lasts one to three years (KG1, KG2 and KG3) and is financed privately because there has been no government policy on pre-schooling until recently.
Basic formal education starts at age six and lasts 12 years, consisting of eight years in primary school and four in high school or secondary.

Primary school is free in public schools and those attending can join a vocational youth/village polytechnic, or make their own arrangements for an apprenticeship program and learn a trade such as tailoring, carpentry, motor vehicle repair, brick-laying and masonry for about two years.

Those who complete high school can join a ___E:polytechnic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_technology)___ or other technical college and study for three years, or proceed directly to university and study for four years.

Graduates from the polytechnics and colleges can then join the workforce and later obtain a specialised higher diploma qualification after a further one to two years of training, or join the university—usually in the second or third year of their respective course.

The ___E:higher diploma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_diploma)___ is accepted by many employers in place of a bachelor's degree and direct or accelerated admission to post-graduate studies is possible in some universities.

Public universities in Kenya are highly commercialised institutions and only a small fraction of qualified high school graduates are admitted on limited government-sponsorship into programs of their choice.
Most are admitted into the social sciences, which are cheap to run, or as self-sponsored students paying the full cost of their studies.
Most qualified students who miss out opt for middle-level diploma programs in public or private universities, colleges, and polytechnics.
In 2018, 18.5 percent of the Kenyan adult population was illiterate, which was the highest rate of literacy in East Africa.

There are very wide regional disparities: for example, Nairobi had the highest level of literacy at 87.1 per cent, compared to North Eastern Province, the lowest, at 8.0 per cent. Preschool, which targets children from age three to five, is an integral component of the education system and is a key requirement for admission to Standard One (First Grade).

Primary school is for students aged 6/7-13/14 years.

For those who proceed to the secondary level, there is a national examination at the end of Form Four – the ___E:Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Certificate_of_Secondary_Education)___ (KCSE), which determines those proceeding to the universities, other professional training, or employment.
Students sit ___E:examinations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Examinations)___ in eight subjects of their choosing.

The Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS), formerly the Joint Admissions Board (JAB), is responsible for selecting students joining the public universities.

Some of Kenya's best-known athletes include the four-time women's ___E:Boston Marathon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Marathon)___ winner and two-time world champion ___E:Catherine Ndereba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Ndereba)___ , 800m world record holder ___E:David Rudisha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Rudisha)___ , former ___E:marathon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport))___ world record-holder ___E:Paul Tergat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tergat)___ , and 5000m Olympic gold medalist ___E:John Ngugi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Ngugi)___ .
Kenya's most decorated athlete is three-time Olympic gold medalist and eleven-time world marathon major champion, ___E:Eliud Kipchoge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge)___ .
Kenya won several medals during the Beijing Olympics: six gold, four silver, and four bronze, making it Africa's most successful nation in the 2008 Olympics.

New athletes gained attention, such as ___E:Pamela Jelimo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Jelimo)___ , the women's 800m gold medalist who went on to win the ___E:IAAF Golden League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_Golden_League)___ jackpot, and ___E:Samuel Wanjiru U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Wanjiru)___ , who won the men's marathon.

Retired Olympic and Commonwealth Games champion ___E:Kipchoge Keino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipchoge_Keino)___ helped usher in Kenya's ongoing distance dynasty in the 1970s and was followed by Commonwealth Champion ___E:Henry Rono U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Rono)___ 's spectacular string of world record performances.

Lately, there has been controversy in Kenyan athletics circles, with the defection of a number of Kenyan athletes to represent other countries, chiefly ___E:Bahrain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain)___ and ___E:Qatar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar)___ .

The Kenyan Ministry of Sports has tried to stop the defections, but they have continued anyway, with ___E:Bernard Lagat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Lagat)___ being the latest, choosing to represent the United States.
Most of these defections occur because of economic or financial factors.
Decisions by the Kenyan government to tax athletes' earnings may also be a motivating factor.
Some elite Kenyan runners who cannot qualify for their country's strong national team find it easier to qualify by running for other countries.
Kenya has been a dominant force in women's volleyball within Africa, with both the clubs and the national team winning various continental championships in the past decade.

Kenyans generally have three meals in a day—breakfast ( kiamsha kinywa ), lunch ( chakula cha mchana ), and supper ( chakula cha jioni or simply chajio ).
In between, they have the 10-o'clock tea ( chai ya saa nne ) and 4 p.m. tea ( chai ya saa kumi ).

Breakfast is usually tea or porridge with bread, ___E:chapati U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapati)___ , ___E:mahamri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamri)___ , boiled sweet potatoes, or ___E:yams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yam_(vegetable))___ . ___E:Githeri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Githeri)___ is a common lunchtime dish in many households, while ___E:Ugali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugali)___ with vegetables, sour milk ( ___E:mursik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mursik)___ ), meat, fish, or any other stew is generally eaten by much of the population for lunch or supper.
Regional variations and dishes also exist.

In western Kenya, among the ___E:Luo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_(Kenya_and_Tanzania))___ , fish is a common dish; among the ___E:Kalenjin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people)___ , who dominate much of the Rift Valley Region, mursik—sour milk—is a common drink.

In cities such as Nairobi, there are fast-food restaurants, including ___E:Steers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steers_(restaurant))___ , ___E:KFC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KFC)___ ,  and ___E:Subway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subway_(restaurant))___ .
There are also many fish-and-chips shops.
___E:Cheese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheese_in_Kenya)___ is becoming more popular in Kenya, with consumption increasing particularly among the middle class.
